Does anyone in your family use a hand fan, what do you call it IN YOUR LANGUAGE, what is it MADE OF. The naming question is the regional-variety half of C-4.2-LO-1; the material question is C-4.2-LO-2. Both cited because the item asks both. Not C-4.3-LO-2 (craft vocabulary carrying community knowledge), which would need the student to explain what the word carries, not just supply it.

Fill the pankha table: state against type of fan against material -- Rajasthan applique and zardozi, brass temple fans, Gujarat mirror work, Kutch leather, West Bengal sola, UP zari and satin, Bihar bamboo. Regional varieties (LO-1) plus traditional materials (LO-2); the table's two columns are precisely those two outcomes. DEFECT: the stem begins mid-glossary ('initiatives ii. actions to improve a situation') and ends with 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube'.

The sub-questions ask for a true/false against what the passage actually says, why the writer chose the word 'traditional', and why 'They were considered exotic and stylish' is opinion rather than fact. That is evaluating supplied material -- C-3.1. Not C-2.1-LO-5, which needs the informative prose to be set against the accompanying short story; no comparison is asked here. Not C-4.2-LO-2, because the content about trade routes is only the vehicle for a fact-versus-opinion exercise.

Infer a negative impact of technology on the pankha, and complete 'the writer refers to pankhas not just as an object but as a CULTURE because ...'. The second sub-question is C-4.3-LO-1 word for word -- the craft standing for a shared cultural identity. Not C-4.2-LO-2: the decorative role is not what is asked, the threat to identity is.

How the title 'Winds of Change' captures the chapter's essence -- needs the metaphor read (C-2.2, close reading of form and style) and the fan's passage from daily utility to decorative artefact (C-4.2-LO-2). C-2.2-LO-12 is deliberately NOT cited: it is the metaphor in 'Canvas of Soil', a different piece in the chapter.

Evaluate how balancing traditional craftsmanship with innovative design will keep the pankha from losing its presence. A preservation-of-the-craft judgement, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-3.2, which is for weighing the premises of supplied argumentative material; nothing here is being argued against.

How pankha-making workshops contribute to preserving the craft -- awareness, technique passed to new learners, livelihood. C-4.3-LO-1's 'efforts to preserve a craft'. Not C-4.2-LO-2: no material or design is in question.

Assess how celebrating pankhas benefits artisans and the craft -- pride, recognition, demand, sustained practice. Still the preservation outcome, C-4.3-LO-1, but from the recognition side rather than the teaching side of the previous item. Not C-3.1: nothing supplied is being evaluated, the student reasons about consequences.

How restricting the pankha to decorative use reflects its CHANGING CULTURAL ROLE -- the second clause of C-4.2-LO-2 exactly. Not C-4.3-LO-1, which is about preservation efforts rather than the role itself. DEFECT: the answer is truncated into an advert -- 'due to the advent Click Here to Buy book on Flipkart'.

'Change' in the title highlights that the fan EVOLVED over centuries -- the sequence of roles it has held, C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-2.2: the option set tests the historical fact, not the figure of speech (the device itself is asked in a separate item).

The hand fan was originally born out of PURE NECESSITY -- the object's origin, which belongs with the etymology-and-history half of C-4.2-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2: necessity is a utilitarian beginning, not one of the decorative or cultural roles LO-2 lists.
Hot climatic conditions made the fan an essential daily item -- why the object arose, so the history strand of C-4.2-LO-1. Not C-4.3-LO-1: nothing about identity or preservation.
Used in ancient royal courts and everyday HOUSEHOLDS -- two settings the fan has occupied, i.e. the roles it has held, C-4.2-LO-2. Not LO-1: no region or etymology is involved.
Fans became highly valued CULTURAL GOODS -- the cultural role named in C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-4.3-LO-1, which needs the preservation-of-identity argument rather than the fact of the status.
Because of their unique DESIGNS they were considered exotic and stylish -- design plus decorative standing, C-4.2-LO-2.

Why fans travelled the ancient trade routes -- because they were valued as exotic cultural goods with intricate designs. Designs and cultural role together, C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-4.2-LO-1: no particular region is at issue.

Different villages created their own UNIQUE VERSIONS -- the existence of regional varieties, which is C-4.2-LO-1's second clause stated in general. Not LO-2, which would need the materials or designs themselves.

The materials and designs of a local fan reflect a region's CULTURAL IDENTITY -- the craft-equals-identity link, C-4.3-LO-1. Chosen over C-4.2-LO-2 because the answer turns on identity, not on what the fan is made of.
Which state's royal heritage the zardozi fan reflects (Rajasthan) -- a state matched to its variety, C-4.2-LO-1. Not LO-2: the material is not asked, the region is.
Zardozi fans are crafted with GOLD THREADS -- a traditional material, C-4.2-LO-2. Distinguished from the previous item, which asked for the state rather than the stuff.

Rajasthan is also known for engraved BRASS temple fans -- a state paired with one of its varieties, C-4.2-LO-1. DEFECT: the answer field runs on into an unrelated collocation drill ('The interviewer asked the candidate to (take/have) a seat', 'My scooter (dashed against/ran into) a car'), which belongs to the C-2.2-LO-14 exercise several items later.

The stem defines the present perfect from 'this handicraft HAS TRANSFORMED into a commercial business' and then has the student fill a paragraph in that tense. C-2.2-LO-13 names exactly this -- the present perfect connecting past craft practice with its present survival. DEFECT: the answer field does not answer the fill-ins; it holds a single unrelated sentence ('In modern times, pankhas have become traditional craft items in India').

Classify word pairs by Appearance / Place / Material ('exotic and stylish', 'within and outside', 'thread and wool') and find more in the text. Collocations and fixed expressions, C-2.2-LO-14. Not C-4.2-LO-2, although one pair names materials: the exercise is about the paired form, not the fan.

Match meanings to word pairs -- high and dry, cut and run, facts and figures, all and sundry, wear and tear. Fixed expressions used correctly, the first half of C-2.2-LO-14. Not C-4.3-LO-2, which is about craft vocabulary; none of these belong to the craft.

The live task is 'make your own hand fan ... display them in class and DESCRIBE THE PROCESS used to make it' -- a description of a familiar object the student has just built, which is what C-1.3-LO-1 covers; it is the only writing LO in this chapter. Not C-2.2-LO-12 despite the concept tag: nothing about metaphor is asked. DEFECTS: the stem opens with a block about framing Madhubani paintings that belongs to another item, the answer is the bare heading 'Process of Making a Paper Hand Fan :', and the concept tag reads "Metaphor in 'Canvas of Soil'".

What literary device the chapter's TITLE uses (metaphor). C-2.2-LO-12 is restricted to the metaphor in 'Canvas of Soil' and the devices in that piece, so it cannot be cited for the chapter title -- hence the C-2.2 competency. Reported as a frame gap: the chapter has no LO for the title's figurative language.

What 'winds' refers to in the title (the cool breeze) -- reading the literal term inside the metaphor. Same reasoning as the previous item: LO-12 belongs to 'Canvas of Soil', so C-2.2 competency. Not C-4.2-LO-2, which would need the fan's role rather than the word's sense.

With cooling no longer needed, the ancient craft risked FADING AWAY -- the threat that makes preservation an issue, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2: the question is about the craft's survival, not about a role it took on.

Did the fan disappear entirely -- no, its ROLE SIMPLY SHIFTED. The change of role is C-4.2-LO-2's second clause. Distinguished from the previous item, which is about the risk of loss rather than the shift.
Elevated from a basic cooling tool to a DECORATIVE ARTEFACT -- the decorative role named in C-4.2-LO-2.

People buy them to decorate homes and to celebrate INDIAN HERITAGE. The heritage-and-identity motive puts it at C-4.3-LO-1 rather than C-4.2-LO-2, which would fit if the answer stopped at 'decoration'.

The shift in usage turned the handicraft into a COMMERCIAL BUSINESS -- another of the roles the fan has held, C-4.2-LO-2. Not C-4.3-LO-1: commercialisation is stated as a fact here, not argued as a preservation strategy.

The economic effect of demand for decorative fans -- a steady, sustainable livelihood for artisans. Livelihood is what keeps the practising community alive, so the preservation outcome C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2, which concerns the object's roles rather than the artisans' survival.
The chapter closes on the importance of PROTECTING THE CRAFT -- C-4.3-LO-1 in a single phrase. Not C-4.2-LO-1: no region or etymology.

Artisans must balance ancient technique with INNOVATIVE DESIGNS to survive -- a preservation strategy, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2, whose designs are the traditional ones. DEFECT: answer field ends 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon PAGE 356 CBSE CLASS 9 ENGLISH R1'.

GUJARAT fans carry beads and mirror work -- a state matched to its regional variety, C-4.2-LO-1. Cited there rather than LO-2 to keep the state-to-variety items together; the material is only the identifying mark.
The spade-shaped fans of KERALA are made of palm leaves -- state plus variety, C-4.2-LO-1.
WEST BENGAL uses the spongy centre of the sola plant -- state plus variety, C-4.2-LO-1.
BIHAR crafts fans from bamboo -- state plus variety, C-4.2-LO-1.
Which state makes woven cane fans (ASSAM) -- state plus variety, C-4.2-LO-1.

A which-statements-are-correct item about state-to-material pairings, so C-4.2-LO-1. DEFECT: the stem holds only ONE of the three statements ('West Bengal uses the sola plant.') while the options refer to statements 1, 2 and 3 -- statements 1 and 2 were dropped in extraction, leaving the key ('only 1 and 3') unverifiable from the row.

The indigenous creators are described as highly HARDWORKING -- the question is about the community that practises the craft, which C-4.3-LO-1 covers. Not C-4.2-LO-2: no material, design or role of the object is asked.

The major threat to the culture of traditional fans is MODERN TECHNOLOGY -- the threat that makes preservation necessary, C-4.3-LO-1. Note the stem says 'culture', not 'use', which is what separates it from the next item.

Electric fans and ACs cut the NEED for hand fans -- the loss of the utilitarian role, which is the role-change clause of C-4.2-LO-2. Distinguished from the previous item, which asks about the threat to the culture rather than to the use.

Introduce yourself as the fan you chose: features, what you like about yourself, your weakness, what makes you unique. A description of a familiar object built from precise detail rather than general praise -- C-1.3-LO-1 exactly. Not C-1.2: the LO exists and names this task type, so competency level would be a loss of precision.

New creative designs are necessary for artisans to appeal to TODAY'S BUYERS -- innovation as the means of keeping the craft alive, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.2-LO-2, whose designs are the traditional inherited ones; these are new.
